headline: Grade A vacancy is just 1.9% across central London (1.3% in both the West End and City), even though overall vacancy figures range from 6.3% to 8.6% depending on the broker.
summary: Avison Young reports central London vacancy unchanged at 6.3% in Q2 2026, the lowest since the pandemic, while JLL's measure stands at 8.6%; BNP Paribas RE reported 8.4% for Q1 2026. The gap reflects definitional differences, but every source shows a market tightening at the top end: Grade A vacancy is 1.9% (up 40bp q/q) and only 1.3% in both the West End and the City. Midtown is the tightest submarket at 4.3% (down 60bp).
insights: Brokers disagree on the overall level (6.3% Avison Young vs 8.6% JLL), but agree on the direction: a tight market for quality space.
Midtown (4.3%) is now the lowest-vacancy submarket in London, according to Avison Young.
CoStar reports that Docklands Core vacancy hit 18.6% in recent months, a record since 2003, which suggests East London is diverging from the core.

signals.title: Grade A scarcity in West End and City
signals.rationale: Grade A vacancy of 1.3% leaves occupiers few options, supporting pre-lets and rental growth for deliveries over 2026-2028.

signals.title: Docklands vacancy at record high
signals.rationale: Record Docklands Core vacancy (CoStar) points to value and letting risk for Canary Wharf / Isle of Dogs assets, particularly second-hand space.
